speaker: Doctor
text:
Can you tell me if you noticed any specific symptoms, like weakness in your legs or trouble speaking, before you started having difficulty walking and losing bladder control?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Spine
REQUEST TEST: EMG

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: I must clarify that cellulitis is a bacterial skin infection and cannot explain your neurological symptoms; could you tell me if you have experienced any loss of sensation or bowel incontinence as well? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain and Cervical Spine.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain and Spinal Cord: Multiple areas of atrophy and signal changes in the brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia, consistent with neurodegenerative processes; Cervical Spine: No focal compressive lesions or myelopathic changes identified.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA). The combination of cerebellar/brainstem atrophy, extrapyramidal signs (rigidity, tremor), autonomic dysfunction (orthostatic hypotension, incontinence), and the absence of spinal cord compression confirms this neurodegenerative disorder.
